architectural_units.description: The administrator is a user with additional permissions to manage application access.

architectural_units.description: The business logic layer applies the domain rules.

architectural_units.name: Portal

architectural_units.name: Spring Boot
architectural_units.description: Spring Boot is a framework that simplifies the creation of Java applications based on Spring, used for the backEnd.

architectural_units.name: Amazon Web Services
architectural_units.description: The provider for this project is Amazon Web Services which has a wide catalog of cloud services and resources.

architectural_units.name: HTTP
architectural_units.description: The message exchange protocol used in this case is HTTP.

architectural_units.name: JSON
architectural_units.description: The data format used is JSON.
The Leader microservice has as its main function the routing of all communications to the corresponding microservice within the system architecture.

The portal microservice has as its main function to offer a centralized interface for access to the different VWGS applications. [...] In each portal, the relevant authentication and authorization controls are carried out with the help of the Leader which decides to which functional domain each user should be routed.
The Communication Log microservice has as its main purpose to record all communications that occur within the system, both between microservices and with external services.

The client, which we also call frontEnd, is responsible for the presentation and user experience of the application, encapsulating the interface logic and the coordination of calls to the server's API.

The controllers, by means of specific functions, process the received requests, manage the validation of the information and channel the requests to the corresponding modules or services of the data layer.
The services offer the interface and the implementation of all the business logic of the application. [...] these call the corresponding functions to obtain the result of the request.
Finally, the Repositories are in charge of performing queries on the database.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The application has an architecture based on microservices, which consists of dividing the system into a set of small, independent, and autonomous services where each microservice is responsible for a specific functionality.

patterns.name: Cloud Architecture
patterns.description: The application is designed, deployed, and executed using cloud services (cloud computing) instead of local or physical servers.

patterns.name: Client-Server
patterns.description: The application follows the Client-Server pattern which organizes the code into two differentiated components: the client, which formulates service requests, and the server, which receives, processes, and returns responses.

patterns.name: MVVM
patterns.description: Angular applies the MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) pattern, as its architecture is based on components and services.

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: Spring Boot organizes the code following the layered pattern with which responsibilities are separated: the presentation layer receives requests and builds responses, the business logic layer applies domain rules, the data access layer interacts with the database, and the domain layer defines the data model.
